section.title: Yahatatastonake and the limits of representation
section.text: Brucie Porter’s biography of Yahatatastonake, known to British officials as The Mortar, identifies him as a representative of Abihka. It follows his efforts to negotiate trade and resist colonial encroachment amid competing British, French and Spanish interests. At the 1765 Pensacola congress, he initially questioned speaking for Upper Creek towns whose leaders were absent. This episode helps explain why an individual leader’s participation should not be treated as agreement by every town. Porter’s account is a later scholarly synthesis; the underlying diplomatic papers remain a separate research task.
